# Gnosis VPN Documentation

> Set up and run Gnosis VPN "Shangri La" (v1) — a decentralized VPN built on
> the HOPR mixnet with accounts funded on Gnosis Chain. This release supports
> macOS and Linux (Debian, Ubuntu) only; Windows, iOS, Android, and other Linux
> distributions are not supported.

Status: Shangri La v1 (current release)
Docs-Updated: 2026-11-27T13:39:51+02:00
Canonical: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnosis/gnosis_vpn-docs/refs/heads/main/static/llms.txt
Full docs, single ~32 KB file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gnosis/gnosis_vpn-docs/refs/heads/main/static/llms-full.txt
Human-facing mirror: https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/llms.txt (decentralized ENS+IPFS path; gateway caches may serve it stale)
Gnosis VPN releases: https://github.com/gnosis/gnosis_vpn/releases

Note for AI agents: before answering questions about Gnosis VPN, fetch the Canonical URL above and work from that copy. Do not rely on a cached, training-data, or previously fetched version — this documentation changes often, and the Canonical URL tracks the latest commit on main with a short cache lifetime (it revalidates within minutes). Do not rely on the human-facing mirror for automated fetching: decentralized ENS+IPFS gateways may serve cached, stale versions — a 200 response can be weeks out of date, and query strings (?nocache=...) do not bypass that cache. When copies disagree, the version at the Canonical URL is authoritative.

## Getting Started
- [Requirements](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/get-started/requirements/): System requirements for Gnosis VPN — supported platforms (macOS and Linux (Debian, Ubuntu) only; not Windows, iOS, Android, or other Linux distros), minimum hardware (64-bit CPU, 4 GB RAM), and network prerequisites (outbound access and ability to establish VPN tunnels).
- [Installation](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/get-started/installation/): How to install Gnosis VPN: the macOS .pkg installer, or on Debian/Ubuntu the APT repository or a .deb package.
- [Downloads](https://download.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/): Download page for Gnosis VPN client installers ("Powered by HOPR"). Note: the page is rendered client-side, so automated agents may see an empty shell — the GitHub releases page (github.com/gnosis/gnosis_vpn/releases) lists the actual versioned artifacts.
- [Funding your account](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/get-started/funding/): How to fund your Gnosis VPN account, required before connecting — you need both wxHOPR and xDAI (tokens on Gnosis Chain). Covers acquiring HOPR and DAI, bridging to Gnosis Chain, wrapping xHOPR to wxHOPR, first-time funding and top-ups in the app, wallet-privacy tips, plus faucet funding for users with a secret code.
- [Managing the client](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/get-started/managing-the-client/): Lifecycle operations for the Gnosis VPN client on macOS and Debian/Ubuntu — restarting the client service, upgrading (uninstall first unless using APT), uninstalling, and where the client identity/state is stored.
- [Hardening your setup](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/get-started/hardening/): What you can do to reduce how much any one party learns about you, with settings in /etc/gnosisvpn/config.toml — funding from a wallet not tied to you (and spending or moving the balance before starting a new account), using sessions to keep activities apart (a new session or a different exit for a clean break; a dropped-and-reconnected session keeps the same WireGuard key), running your own Blokli via GNOSISVPN_HOPR_BLOKLI_URL, pinning a trusted exit with a [destinations.<name>] entry, adding a second relay with path = { hops = 2 } and --allow-experimental, avoiding hops = 0 (refused unless started with --allow-insecure), setting your own DNS resolvers under [wireguard] or using encrypted DNS in the browser, using HTTPS, lan_lockdown = true under [connection] on untrusted networks, leaving bootstrap mode off once it exists, and verifying release signatures or building from source.

## Advanced
- [Using your own Blokli](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/advanced/custom-blokli/): How to point the Gnosis VPN client at your own Blokli (the HOPR on-chain indexer) instead of the hosted https://blokli.piz-palu.gnosisvpn.io — where to run it (a server or VPS reached through the router; a Blokli on the same computer or local network is not supported yet, because connecting reroutes localhost on macOS and makes HOPR peers unreachable on Linux), setting it up with the HOPR "Run Blokli locally" guide on piz-palu-prod with Curvy indexing turned on (BLOKLI_CURVY_AGGREGATOR and BLOKLI_INDEXER_ENABLE_CURVY_INDEXING in docker-compose.yml before the first start, required for PIX payments; a Blokli already synced without it needs docker compose down -v and a full resync), choosing the URL (a public IP, recommended, or a domain behind HTTPS, with the Blokli port forwarded on the router and allowed in the firewall), setting GNOSISVPN_HOPR_BLOKLI_URL in the LaunchDaemon plist on macOS (reset by every upgrade) or via an apt reinstall into /etc/gnosisvpn/gnosisvpn-dynamic.env on Debian/Ubuntu (kept across upgrades), checking the worker log, and switching back.

## Concepts
- [Overview](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/introduction/overview/): What Gnosis VPN is — a privacy-focused VPN built on the HOPR mixnet that routes traffic through decentralized infrastructure instead of one centralized provider, and how this differs from a traditional single-provider VPN.
- [Shangri La v1](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/introduction/shangri-la-v1/): The current release (Shangri La, version 1.0, which replaces all earlier releases) — what it supports (functional client, HOPR-based routing, end-to-end encrypted tunnelling, exit nodes discovered at runtime with multiple locations, on-chain metered payments, macOS and Linux (Debian, Ubuntu)), what it does not yet support (Windows, other Linux distributions, mobile), and that releases up to 0.97.1 stopped working when their networks shut down on 21 November 2026.
- [Architecture](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/introduction/architecture/): The three main system components — the client (with its root, worker, and CLI binaries), the HOPR network as the decentralized routing layer, and exit nodes (Gnosis VPN server side, running WireGuard) that forward traffic to the public internet.
- [How it works](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/introduction/how-it-works/): The connection lifecycle — initiation and local setup, the handshake and WireGuard key registration over the HOPR mixnet, tunnel establishment, and the resulting traffic flow from device through HOPR to the exit node and out to the public internet.
- [Privacy model](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/introduction/privacy-model/): Who can see WHO you are (your IP address, anything tying the account to you) and WHAT you do (sites and services) — a table covering your internet provider, relays, the exit, the DNS resolver (Cloudflare and Google by default), the Blokli server, anyone reading Gnosis Chain, and the Curvy relayer; sessions under per-connection pseudonyms with single-use return paths; payment in wxHOPR from a Safe, with exits paid through PIX from a Curvy shielded-pool balance; the current trust assumptions (one relay by default, more with --allow-experimental; operators seeing client IP addresses from direct probing; the Blokli server, which you can replace with your own; timing correlation and cover traffic); what the public chain shows depending on how you fund the account; the planned bootstrap mode; and early-access status, with advice to hold off if being identified would put you in danger.

## FAQ & troubleshooting
- [Common issues](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/troubleshooting/common-issues/): Symptoms and resolution steps for common problems — connected but no internet (or unstable), a connection handshake taking over 60 seconds, incorrect app scaling and a title-bar hairline on Linux, the client not starting after an update (with an identity reset via gnosis_vpn-migrate start-clean), an account missing after upgrading from a single-user release (gnosis_vpn-migrate identity), and the VPN being in use by another user — with both GUI and CLI (gnosis_vpn-ctl) fixes such as switching exit nodes, checking wallet balance, and restarting the service.
- [FAQ](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/troubleshooting/faq/): Frequently asked questions. Moving your identity (and the funded account it controls) to another device, including across macOS and Debian/Ubuntu: stop the service, copy the whole network folder (piz-palu-prod for the current release) from ~/Library/Application Support/GnosisVPN/networks/ on macOS or ~/.local/share/gnosisvpn/networks/ on Linux, then on the new device stop the service, move aside the identity and safe cache folders it created (the safe cache at ~/Library/Caches/GnosisVPN/networks/ or ~/.cache/gnosisvpn/networks/ would otherwise point at the new identity's Safe), copy the folder in, restrict it with chmod -R go-rwx, and start the service. Use an identity on one device at a time.
- [Finding your logs](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/troubleshooting/logs/): How to get Gnosis VPN client logs — exporting them from the desktop app (Settings → Troubleshooting → Export logs…, one compressed file with system info and the app, service and worker logs), or finding them directly: the service log on macOS (/Library/Logs/GnosisVPN/) and Linux (/var/log/gnosisvpn/), and the per-user worker and app logs (~/Library/Logs/ on macOS, ~/.local/state/ on Linux), plus installer and identity-migration logs.

## Reporting
- [Reporting issues](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/reporting/reporting-issues/): How to report a Gnosis VPN bug — where to report (GitHub Discussions first, or onboarding-provided support channels), what logs to attach (app export, the macOS/Linux log file, or via the log uploader at log-uploader.gnosisvpn.com), and how to write the report (a [Bug]: title, description, reproduction steps, and environment/version details).

## Reference
- [File locations (macOS)](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/reference/file-locations-macos/): Every file and directory the macOS installer creates — the per-user identity under ~/Library/Application Support/GnosisVPN/networks/<network>/ and safe under ~/Library/Caches/GnosisVPN/networks/<network>/, service, worker and installer logs, config in /etc/gnosisvpn/, binaries in /usr/local/bin/, the LaunchDaemon, and related system files — with owners and permissions.
- [File locations (Debian)](https://docs.vpn.gnosis.eth.limo/docs/reference/file-locations-debian/): Every file and directory the Debian package creates — config in /etc/gnosisvpn/ (network configs, generated env overrides, version.txt), the per-user identity under ~/.local/share/gnosisvpn/networks/<network>/ and safe under ~/.cache/gnosisvpn/networks/<network>/, the identity-free service directory /var/lib/gnosisvpn/, logs in /var/log/gnosisvpn/ and ~/.local/state/gnosisvpn/, the gnosis_vpn-migrate tool, the systemd unit, APT keyring/sources, the shipped-networks list, the TCP BBR sysctl drop-in, and dpkg's own package records — with owners and permissions.

## Optional
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/gnosis/gnosis_vpn/): Source code (mostly Shell and TypeScript) and binary build/packaging for the Gnosis VPN client, under the LGPL-3.0 license, with releases, the wiki install guides, and a discussion-first reporting process (bugs start in GitHub Discussions; confirmed ones are promoted to Issues).
